tema: The Big Bang and the Age of the Universe
palavras: the big bang and the age of the universe
resposta: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old. The Big Bang wasn't an explosion at one point, but the expansion of all space from an extremely hot, dense state.
aprofundar: This is backed up by strong evidence: the cosmic microwave background radiation, the spacing of galaxies, and the amount of hydrogen and helium in the cosmos. What was before, if there was one before, no one knows. The priest and physicist Georges Lemaître proposed the idea of the primordial atom in 1927 and 1931. Practice: look at the dark sky tonight; some of that light went out before the Earth existed.
camada3: To contemplate: Did the universe have a beginning, or did time begin with it? If time was born there, the question of what existed before may not have made sense. Stay with the wonder.

resposta: Dark matter is something invisible that has gravity. We know it exists because of the effects: galaxies spin too fast for the matter we can see.
aprofundar: It would make up about 27 percent of the universe, compared with about 5 percent of ordinary matter. What it is, no one knows: no dark matter particle has been detected to date. To know that something exists without knowing what it is: that is an honest mystery.
camada3: To contemplate: Most of the matter in the universe is invisible to us. How much of your own life is gravity acting on, not showing up? The invisible also rules.

resposta: In 1998, it was discovered that the expansion of the universe is accelerating. The cause has been dubbed dark energy, about 68 percent of everything that exists.
aprofundar: The discovery won him the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics. But dark energy is a name for our ignorance: we don't yet know what it is, or whether it's constant in time.
camada3: To contemplate: Seventy percent of everything has a name and no explanation. Honest science lives with that without inventing. Can you live with your open-ended questions?

resposta: A black hole is a region where gravity is so strong that not even light escapes. The boundary without a return is called the event horizon.
aprofundar: In 2019, the Event Horizon telescope showed the first image of the shadow of a black hole, the star M87, 55 million light-years away. Stephen Hawking predicted that black holes emit weak radiation and can evaporate, but this has not yet been observed. What happens at the center, in the singularity, is unknown.
camada3: To contemplate: on the event horizon, the laws we know reach their limit. Every mystical tradition also speaks of a point where words stop. What is there beyond what you can say?

resposta: Einstein showed that time does not pass the same for everyone: it runs slower at high speeds and near large masses. That's measured, not imagined.
aprofundar: GPS satellites correct this effect every day; otherwise, they would be miles off course. Traveling into the future, in a way, is possible. For the past, there is no evidence. And what time really is remains one of the greatest mysteries of physics. Einstein wrote, in a 1955 letter to the family of his friend Michele Besso: For us convinced physicists, the distinction between past, present and future is only an illusion, though persistent.
camada3: To contemplate: if time is relative, the now is the only place where you really are. How much of your day did you spend outside of it?

resposta: Life on Earth emerged about 3.5 to 4 billion years ago. How chemistry became biology, called abiogenesis, we still don't know in detail.
aprofundar: There are strong hypotheses, like the world of RNA and hydrothermal vents on the seafloor, and experiments that form life molecules from simple chemistry. But no one has created life from scratch in a lab. The first step remains a mystery.
camada3: To contemplate: out of lifeless chemistry came something that makes you wonder where it came from. That you exist, and know that you exist, is as strange a fact as any miracle.

resposta: We already know of more than 5,000 planets outside the solar system, the exoplanets. Life outside the Earth, however, has not yet been found.
aprofundar: The Fermi paradox asks: If the universe is so big and ancient, where is everyone? Life's empty answers are rare until we've looked hard enough. There is no evidence of alien visitation. The search continues, and the question is legitimate.
camada3: For contemplation: In the movie Contact, based on the book by Carl Sagan, it is said that being alone is a huge waste of space. The question we're alone also speaks to us: How do we treat the only life we know?

resposta: Multiverse is the idea that our universe would be one among many. It comes up in some theories, like eternal inflation and the many-worlds interpretation of quantum physics.
aprofundar: Honesty: it's a hypothesis, it's not proven, and maybe it can't even be tested. There are physicists who defend it and others who say it's not even science. Keep the question open, don't rush to close it.
camada3: To contemplate: even though there are infinite universes, this is the only one in which you can love, choose and act. The greatness of the possibilities does not lessen the weight of your step.

tema: Why there is something rather than nothing
palavras: why there is something rather than nothing
resposta: Why is there something instead of nothing? Leibniz asked that question over three hundred years ago, and it remains unanswered.
aprofundar: Physics explains how the universe evolves, but not why it exists. Religions, philosophies and scientists offer different paths, and none are proof. In the face of such a question, the wisest thing to do is wonder. The philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein wrote in Tractatus: The mystic is not how the world is, but that it is.
camada3: To contemplate: stay a minute just feeling that you exist, without thinking about who you are. This astonishment is the beginning of all philosophy, as Plato said.

resposta: Why does brain matter generate experience, red from red, pain from pain? Philosopher David Chalmers called this the hard problem of consciousness.
aprofundar: Neuroscience maps a lot of what the brain does, but it still doesn't explain why feeling exists. The odds range from materialism to panpsychism, and none have won. You're the mystery that wonders about itself. Practice: for a minute, don't pay attention to things, pay attention to the fact that you perceive things.
camada3: To contemplate: the Upanishads say that what you see cannot be seen, what you know cannot be known as an object. You can search for consciousness; you will never find it as a thing, because it is with it that you search.

palavras: where do the atoms come from
resposta: The carbon in his body, the iron in his blood and the calcium in his bones were forged into stars. You are literally star dust.
aprofundar: Hydrogen and helium came from the Big Bang. The heaviest elements were born from fusion within stars, from supernovae and from collisions of neutron stars. Carl Sagan said, we are a way for the cosmos to know itself.
camada3: To contemplate: the atoms of your body have been in stars and will be in other things after you. What about you isn't borrowed?

palavras: what is the size of the universe
resposta: The observable universe is about 93 billion light-years across. And there could be a lot more beyond what we can see.
aprofundar: It's larger than 13.8 billion light-years because space kept expanding as light traveled. It is estimated that there are hundreds of billions to trillions of galaxies. Whether the entire universe is finite or infinite, no one knows. Pascal wrote: The eternal silence of these infinite spaces terrifies me. And again: by space the universe embraces me; by thought I embrace it.
camada3: To contemplate: you are tiny in space and yet the universe fits in your mind. Both things are true at the same time.

resposta: The Sun is a star about 4.6 billion years old. At its core, nuclear fusion turns hydrogen into helium and releases the light that sustains life.
aprofundar: Light that leaves the surface of the sun takes about eight minutes and twenty seconds to reach you. It should shine for another five billion years. Every morning, you receive an energy born in the heart of a star.
camada3: To contemplate: Almost every tradition has honored the sun as a symbol of consciousness that illuminates no matter who it chooses. Plotinus wrote that the eye would never see the Sun if it were not itself similar to the Sun. What light do you offer without asking for anything in return?

resposta: Gravitational waves are ripples in space-time itself. Einstein predicted them in 1916, and the LIGO observatory first detected them in 2015.
aprofundar: The signal came from the merger of two black holes over a billion light years away. The measured deformation was less than a thousandth of a proton. The discovery won the 2017 Nobel Prize: for the first time, we heard the universe.
camada3: To contemplate: for billions of years the universe vibrated and no one heard. How many things in your life are talking and you still don't have the instrument to listen to?

resposta: How the universe will end, no one knows for sure. The most widely accepted scenario today is an eternal expansion into a dark cold, thermal death, trillions of trillions of years from now.
aprofundar: Other scenarios are the Big Rip, where everything tears, and the Big Crunch, where everything contracts. The answer depends on dark energy, which we still don't understand. None of this threatens you: these are unimaginable times.
camada3: To contemplate: if not even the stars are eternal, the value of things is not in lasting forever. It lies in shining while they exist.

palavras: we are one with the universe
resposta: A reflection, not a science: the same atoms that make up stars make up you. The universe isn't just out there; it's also thinking through you.
aprofundar: This is a contemplative bridge. Science shows the common origin of matter; the meaning you give to it is your choice. Look at the sky tonight and remember: you are part of what you observe.
camada3: To contemplate: Carl Sagan said that we are a way for the cosmos to know itself. If that's true, every time you contemplate, the universe contemplates itself.

resposta: Free will is one of the oldest questions: are we free or is everything already determined? Philosophy and neuroscience are still debating, and no one has the final answer.
aprofundar: Benjamin Libet's experiments in the 1980s measured brain activity before conscious decision-making, but their interpretation is much debated. Espinosa thought we think we're free because we don't know the causes that drive us. Inner reading: freedom may be knowing these causes. Practice: Today, before you react, count to three and choose.
camada3: To contemplate: even without a final answer, living as the author of one's own choices brings more responsibility and more peace. Between the stimulus and the response there is a space; in that space lives your freedom.
